extraction_notes: MetLife Group Critical Illness proposal, Attained Age rate structure. Layout: Cover page has group name/dates. Rate tables appear on pages 6-7 titled "Premium Structure – Low Plan" and "Premium Structure – High Plan" - these are TWO separate products/plan tiers (low benefit choice vs high benefit choice, corresponding to the $10,000 and $20,000 GI benefit amounts mentioned in Plan Design section on page 4). Each plan table has identical structure: 4 coverage-class columns (Employee Only, Employee + Spouse, Employee + Children, Employee + Spouse/Children) and 14 attained-age row bands: <25, 25-29, 30-34, 35-39, 40-44, 45-49, 50-54, 55-59, 60-64, 65-69, 70-74, 75-79, 80-84, 85-99. Rates are printed as "per $1,000 of coverage" - actual premium = rate x (benefit amount/1000). In this document, the Low Plan and High Plan tables had IDENTICAL rate values (both used same per-$1000 rate schedule) - still extract both as separate products since they are distinct plan designs/benefit tiers, do not merge. Note: rate table columns are NOT dollar coverage amounts but rather relationship/class tiers - store rate as key "per_1000" in rates_by_amount since actual amount depends on elected benefit ($10k or $20k for employee, 50% of that for spouse/child). Plan design details: GI benefit choice of $10,000 or $20,000 for employee; spouse gets 50% of employee amount, child(ren) get 50% of employee amount; Total Benefit Amount = 300% of initial benefit; covered conditions include Coronary Artery Bypass Graft, Full Benefit Cancer, Partial Benefit Cancer, Heart Attack, Kidney Failure, Major Organ Transplant, Stroke (with initial/recurrence benefit percentages on page 5 - not part of rate grid). Total products in doc: Critical Illness (2 plan tiers: Low, High) - other products (e.g. life, disability) may appear in other MetLife bundles but were not present here. Each plan tier has 4 classes, no separate 'Child' only class - children always bundled into 'Employee + Children' or 'Employee + Spouse/Children' class labels. No flat-rate classes - all age-banded.
